key_insight: After a dementia diagnosis, both people living with MCI/AD/ADRD and their care partners need ongoing, personalized help with daily care, navigation, and emotional support—not just one-time information.
clinical_relevance: Post-diagnostic support programs and AI tools may be more useful if they address practical care questions, care partner strain, and resource navigation over time.
method: 11 community-dwelling dementia dyads plus 1 additional care partner were interviewed
12 dementia care experts from academic medical centers, clinics, and aging organizations were also interviewed
Researchers used semi-structured interviews and conventional content analysis
evidence_signal: This was a qualitative interview study, so the evidence shows common needs and themes rather than testing whether an intervention improves outcomes.
watch_item: An AI chatbot may need careful design for cultural responsiveness, safety, privacy, and clear escalation pathways because needs are complex and change over time.
paper_title: Navigating Life After Dementia Diagnosis: Questions, Challenges, and Support Needs Among Dementia Dyads
